result.topic_en: Euler shows that when Z = 𝔷q (with 𝔷 a function of x, y, p), or more generally for the integral ∫(Z + 𝔷q)dx, the Euler–Lagrange equation reduces to second order, and then introduces the third class where Z depends on x, y, p, q.
result.transcription:
VARIATIONVM TRACTANDI. 67

51. Praeterea vero etiam ad ſecundam claſſem referri oportet caſus, quibus $Z=\mathfrak{Z}q$ exiſtente $\mathfrak{Z}$ functione quacunque ipſarum $x$, $y$ et $p$, ſi enim fuerit
$d\mathfrak{Z}=\mathfrak{M}dx+\mathfrak{N}dy+\mathfrak{P}dp$
habebimus
$M=\mathfrak{M}q;\ N=\mathfrak{N}q;\ P=\mathfrak{P}q,$ et $Q=\mathfrak{Z}$
quare quum aequatio pro curua ſit
$0=N-\frac{dP}{dx}+\frac{ddQ}{dx^2}$, ſiue $0=N-\frac{1}{dx}d.\left(P-\frac{dQ}{dx}\right);$
formula haec $P-\frac{dQ}{dx}$ abit in
$\mathfrak{P}q-\frac{d\mathfrak{Z}}{dx}=\mathfrak{P}q-\mathfrak{M}-\mathfrak{N}p-\mathfrak{P}q=-\mathfrak{M}-\mathfrak{N}p$
vnde aequatio noſtra euadet
$0=N+\frac{1}{dx}d(\mathfrak{M}+\mathfrak{N}p)=2\mathfrak{N}q+\frac{d\mathfrak{M}}{dx}+p\frac{d\mathfrak{N}}{dx}$,
quae manifeſto tantum differentialia ſecundi gradus continet. Generalius ergo adhuc ſi formula integralis propoſita fuerit $\int(Z+\mathfrak{Z}q)dx$, vbi $Z$ et $\mathfrak{Z}$ quomodocunque ex quantitatibus $x$, $y$ et $p$ ſint compoſitae, aequatio pro curua quaeſita erit
$0=N-\frac{dP}{dx}+2\mathfrak{N}q+\frac{d\mathfrak{M}}{dx}+p\frac{d\mathfrak{N}}{dx}$
ſiue etiam
$0=Ndx-dP+2\mathfrak{N}dp+d\mathfrak{M}+pd\mathfrak{N}$
quae manifeſto tantum eſt differentialis ſecundi gradus.

52. At ſi quantitas $Z$ ita ex litteris $x,y,p$ et $q$ fuerit compoſita vt poſito III. Claſſis.
$dZ=Mdx+Ndy+Pdp+Qdq$
I 2 etiam

items.quote: Praeterea vero etiam ad ſecundam claſſem referri oportet caſus, quibus $Z=\mathfrak{Z}q$ exiſtente $\mathfrak{Z}$ functione quacunque ipſarum $x$, $y$ et $p$
items.english: Moreover, the cases in which Z = 𝔷q, with 𝔷 any function of x, y and p, must also be referred to the second class.

items.quote:
Generalius ergo adhuc ſi formula integralis propoſita fuerit $\int(Z+\mathfrak{Z}q)dx$, vbi $Z$ et $\mathfrak{Z}$ quomodocunque ex quantitatibus $x$, $y$ et $p$ ſint compoſitae, aequatio pro curua quaeſita erit
$0=N-\frac{dP}{dx}+2\mathfrak{N}q+\frac{d\mathfrak{M}}{dx}+p\frac{d\mathfrak{N}}{dx}$
items.english: More generally, if the proposed integral formula is ∫(Z + 𝔷q)dx, where Z and 𝔷 are composed in any way of x, y and p, the equation for the sought curve will be 0 = N − dP/dx + 2𝔑q + d𝔐/dx + p d𝔑/dx, which is only of the second differential order.
